title: introduce-streaming-schema-hints-and-openai-compat-error-mapping-for-toolcalls
author: Asha Kapoor
description: Motivation: Streaming responses that must conform to a declared JSON schema are fragile when the model emits partial tokens or when tool/function calls interleave with the stream. This PR introduces a light-weight schema hinting protocol and a controlled error mapping for OpenAI-compat clients so downstream applications get actionable, stable errors without sacrificing streaming throughput. High-level changes: 1) streaming schema hints: a non-blocking inline hint token ("::schema-hint::") that annotates checkpoints in the stream with incremental validation state and an optional resume_token for safe rewind or resumption; 2) toolcall anchor points: runtime now inserts explicit toolcall-safety anchors around tool/function-calling JSON fragments so the schema validator can skip partial tool JSON until a tool boundary completes; 3) OpenAI-compat error mapping: new structured error codes (RESP_SCHEMA_HINT, RESP_TOOL_BOUNDARY, RESP_PARTIAL_JSON) are mapped to HTTP 400/422 where appropriate and to rich error objects in the OpenAI-compat envelope; 4) graceful fallback policy: when strict mode is off, the runtime will emit a schema-hint with severity=warning instead of terminating the stream, and surface a retry_hint that clients can use to trigger a higher-fidelity generation on the next request. Design notes: The schema-hint is intentionally compact, intended for machine consumption by SDKs and proxies. It contains fields: status(OK|WARN|ERR), path(hierarchical JSON pointer as string), issue_code(short token), message(human readable), resume_token(optional opaque string). Runtime keeps a short-lived resume token store keyed by resume_token with a TTL to enable stream resume or targeted re-generation of the last chunk without redoing the entire prompt. Tool/function calling behavior: toolcall anchors look like special control frames in the stream and are considered atomic for schema validation; partial tool frames are ignored until closed. This prevents false-positive schema errors when a tool emits multi-frame JSON. OpenAI compatibility: the compatibility layer translates our structured error objects into the OpenAI-like error envelope while preserving machine-readable fields under error.metadata. It also adds an opt-in header x-rw-schema-mode with values permissive|strict which influences whether a schema-hint severity=ERR escalates to a hard stream termination. Migration and rollout: default mode remains permissive. We will enable schema hints for 10% of hosted traffic as an opt-in SL rollout, collect telemetry on schema-hint rates and resume_token usage, run performance A/B on latency and throughput, then widen to 100%. QA and testing: unit tests for hint emission under different tokenization scenarios, integration tests for toolcall anchor boundaries, compatibility tests ensuring OpenAI-compat clients receive mapped error envelopes, load tests to validate resume_token store performance under peak burst. Checklist: - [x] implement hint emitter in runtime stream fanout - [x] add toolcall anchor detection and semantics - [x] add resume_token store and APIs - [x] wire into OpenAI-compat adapter with mapped error envelope - [x] add SDK parsing helpers (python/ts) - [x] create integration tests and perf benchmarks - [x] add telemetry counters and dashboards Backwards compatibility: clients that ignore schema-hint tokens will see no behavior change. Strict-mode customers can opt-in to fail-fast behavior via x-rw-schema-mode header or per-route setting. Related work: builds on ENG-1219 (stream snapshot repair) and ENG-1587 (structured output error taxonomy). Release notes: adds streaming schema hint tokens and OpenAI-compat error mapping; no breaking changes by default.

Notable commits: add-schema-hint-emitter, anchor-toolcall-boundaries, resume-token-api, openai-compat-error-mapping, sdk-helpers-python-ts, add-integration-tests
files_changed: runtime/streaming/hint_emitter.py (new) - implements compact hint token emission; runtime/streaming/tool_anchor.py (new) - detection and anchor framing; runtime/validation/schema_checkpoint.py (mod) - incremental validation hooks; runtime/kv/resume_store.go (new) - small in-memory resume token store with TTL; adapters/openai_compat/error_mapper.go (mod) - map structured errors to OpenAI envelope; sdk/python/redwood/schema_hints.py (new) - helper to parse hints; sdk/ts/src/schemaHints.ts (new) - same for TS SDK; tests/integration/test_tool_anchor_stream.py (new); tests/unit/test_schema_hint_roundtrip.py (new); docs/api/streaming_schema_hints.md (new) - docs and examples; telemetry/dashboards/schema_hints_overview.json (new)
discussion: Initial reviewer feedback asked for tighter bounds on resume_token TTL and a sanity limit on resume_store size. I added a configurable default TTL of 5 minutes and a per-tenant 2000-entry cap with LFU eviction. Liam asked to ensure that anchors are still valid across re-encoding (BPE fragmentation); added tests that simulate mid-token boundary splits and validated hint emission aligns with token boundaries where possible. Sophie requested clear guidance in docs for SDKs to ignore hints if not used; added explicit parsing helpers and examples in the Python and TS SDKs. Ravi flagged potential perf regressions on high-throughput streams; ran a dedicated load test that showed a 2% median latency increase under synthetic 10k rps scenarios which was acceptable; optimized hint emission path to avoid allocations and re-ran. All reviewers approved and I squashed and merged after CI green. There was one transient flaky test in CI which was retried and passed.
release_notes: Adds streaming schema hint tokens and OpenAI-compatible structured error mapping for schema and toolcall boundaries. Default behavior is permissive. Customers can opt into strict mode per-route or via x-rw-schema-mode header. SDKs added parsing helpers.
examples: Server stream example: server streams tokens and occasionally emits '::schema-hint::{"status":"WARN","path":"/choices/0/message/content","issue_code":"TRUNCATION","message":"partial object received","resume_token":"rt_abc123"}' at logical checkpoints

Client resume workflow: client receives schema-hint with resume_token then issues a resume request POST /v1/resume with resume_token to receive a targeted re-generation of the last chunk instead of full prompt re-run
notes_for_ops: Resume token store runs as an in-memory sharded service with Redis fallback for private deployments. Default TTL=5m and cap=2000 per tenant. Telemetry counters: schema_hint_emitted, schema_hint_error, resume_token_used, tool_anchor_ignored. Dashboards added under Observability->Structured Output->Schema Hints.
qa_steps: 1) Run unit tests included in PR. 2) Run integration tests: tests/integration/test_tool_anchor_stream.py. 3) Deploy canary to 10% hosted traffic and validate telemetry counters over 1h. 4) Verify OpenAI-compat clients receive error.metadata fields and that permissive mode does not terminate streams. 5) Verify strict mode via header x-rw-schema-mode=strict terminates stream on ERR hints.
